chunks.title: CLO 2025 Course: Create Christmas CP Outfits Together with Little Bear Kedundun!
chunks.content: # CLO 2025 Course: Create Christmas CP Outfits with Little Bear Kedundun This document details the step-by-step process of creating a Christmas outfit using CLO 2025 software, focusing on advanced features such as Glow2025, needle structure customization, fabric application, and pattern generation. It covers technical instructions for garment construction, fabric and stitch settings, pattern design, and simulation optimization. --- ## Introduction to Glow2025 and Real-Time Editor This section introduces the Glow2025 feature in CLO 2025, highlighting its capabilities in real-time editing and version generation. It outlines how to create various needle types including hollow needles, thick needles, and needles without gaps, and how to tie strings within the garment construction process. --- ## Setting Up the Editor and Importing Materials - Create a basic round loop in the editor and modify it. - Open the library window and create a new library. - Import ZPRJ files downloaded from the Connect shopping platform, which contains free basic formats and models. - Select gender and style options; the example uses a V1 model. - Add models to the shopping cart and deliver orders for use without additional downloads. - Drag purchased or free models directly into the workspace. --- ## Modifying Garment Body and Sleeve - Delete excess curve points to simplify the sweater style, which primarily uses straight lines. - Shorten front and back pieces to length 80, adjust straighter lines. - Turn up collar and sleeve edges, adding small box sides and drawstrings. - Adjust sleeve length by pulling down 50 mm and widening by 5 cm. - Use outside board expansion with a diameter of 190 mm to extend sleeve folds. - Sew fold edges using sewing lines and simulate for flatness. - Create small lotus leaf edge on sleeve using folding arrangement tool (width 780 mm, height 23 mm). - Adjust particle diameter of foldable plates to 10 mm and copy to match. --- ## Creating Shoulder Decorative Panels - Draw inner lines with Ctrl key to form curves. - Adjust curves for desired shape and size (600 mm wide, 75 mm high). - Sew decorative panels to sleeves; freeze and place outside. - Add internal line borders of 30 mm to panels; cut and sew. - Duplicate panels symmetrically for the opposite side. --- ## Collar Construction and Folding - Delete original collar and modify collar line. - Use panel outline expansion with shrink option to adjust collar width by 25 mm outward. - Measure neck width (~300 mm) and create half-collar shape with 160 cm width and 180 cm height, adding 20 cm looseness. - Position collar on the model’s neck, freeze before sewing. - Sew front and back collar sides, draw inner line border at 67 mm. - Use folding arrangement tool to fold collar outward. - Simulate and reverse-activate stuck hair in back for better shape. - Solidify shape, reduce volume slightly, and freeze for stability. - Add internal line borders (25 mm) on front and back collar pieces; cut and sew.

The Christmas-themed live replay is here! Join CLO's little bear Kedundun to create your exclusive Christmas outfit!  
CLO technical experts use the latest AI panel generator and fabric editor features in CLO version 2025.2 to guide you step-by-step through the entire process from style creation to modification!  
Follow the official WeChat account "CLO3D" and reply with "free materials" in the message box to receive this edition's resources.

chunks.content: - Measure neck width (~300 mm) and create half-collar shape with 160 cm width and 180 cm height, adding 20 cm looseness. - Position collar on the model’s neck, freeze before sewing. - Sew front and back collar sides, draw inner line border at 67 mm. - Use folding arrangement tool to fold collar outward. - Simulate and reverse-activate stuck hair in back for better shape. - Solidify shape, reduce volume slightly, and freeze for stability. - Add internal line borders (25 mm) on front and back collar pieces; cut and sew. - Use random colors for better visualization during simulation. --- ## Adding Decorative Lines and Fold Lines - Use plus point division tool to add average segments (4 lines) on panels. - Add points at specific positions to create fold lines. - Draw fold lines using internal line tool, ensuring smooth connections. - Set line diameter to 2.5 mm and curve count to 1 for sewing lines. - Sew lines to panels, adjust diameter and hardness for stability. - Duplicate and simulate folded lines for symmetry. --- ## Tie Drawstring Construction - Draw 160 cm internal line on front panel and copy. - Assign diameters of 25 mm and 75 mm to duplicated lines. - Use transverse fold tool and reverse direction for fold effect. - Repeat fold and copy processes for front and back pieces. - Harden panels before sewing to prevent penetration. - Sew folds and simulate natural folds. - Add a transparent panel with opacity set to 1 on support panels. - Adjust panel diagonal from 0 to 10 for better folding. - Use round-shaped board tool to add metal ring with diameter 14 mm and band diameter 3 mm. - Sew metal ring components, freeze, and simulate for placement. - Duplicate and mirror metal ring boards symmetrically on both sides. --- ## Creating Main Body and Tie Boards - Create a small body board with width 30 cm and height 5 mm. - Sew it to the metal ring board, position, and root together. - Duplicate board, lengthen to 40 mm for diagonal adjustment. - Position and sew subsequent boards, ensuring correct sewing sequence. - Use 3D window for sewing to ease visualization. - Adjust interlocking relationships using grid comparison tool. - Add butterfly knot from library; resize and freeze parts to fit string width. - Sew butterfly knot directly and simulate, adjusting for penetration. - Harden metal ring plates and apply grid tools for alignment. - Cut and sew internal lines of metal ring plates. - Set small inner panels as transparent and apply metal ring fabric with gold color. --- ## Needle Fabric Setup and Customization - Total of six needle fabrics used: large body, bottom, sleeve, collar, sleeve decoration strip. - Assign fabrics and names accordingly (e.g., hollow fabric for collar). - Select wool product type and flat needle method. - Use piece editor to adjust thread length, width, thickness, and density.
